conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: REDEFINES clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR16 (cite.py --check 13.18.44.3 'Data-name-2 shall not be described with the ANY LENGTH clause.' OK). ResolveRedefines: `if (item.RedefinesTarget is { IsAnyLength: true }) Edition.Error("COBOLNET1542", ... SR16)`. Probe sr16_anylen2 (contained program, LINKAGE `01 L PIC X ANY LENGTH. 01 M REDEFINES L PIC X(4).`) -> COBOLNET1542 'the redefined item is described with the ANY LENGTH clause (ISO §13.18.44.3 SR16)'. No spec-derived test found - test-needed. (Diagnostic code 1542 is shared with the §13.18.2 placement rule - a catalog-hygiene note, not a verdict issue.) || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ANY LENGTH arrives in 2002)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-2 shall not be described with the ANY LENGTH clause.

rows.subject: RELATIVE KEY clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR1: 'The first logical record has a relative record number of 1, and subsequent logical records have relative record numbers of 2, 3, 4, ...' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.13.4 "The first logical record has a relative record number of 1" -> OK). The runtime store is keyed by 1-based RRN (RelativeConnector.cs:24 slot store, :522 `into.Put(i + 1, rec)`). Probe rk4 (pinned cobol.exe): ACCESS SEQUENTIAL OPEN OUTPUT, three WRITEs with RELATIVE KEY preset to 77 -> key item reads 0001, 0002, 0003 after each (FS 00); sequential READs return AAAA K=0001, BBBB K=0002; DYNAMIC random READ with key 0 -> INVALID KEY, FS=23; random WRITE with key 0 -> FS=34, which is what §14.9.51.4 GR29 b) requires for a value less than 1 (cite.py --find located it: §14.9.51.4 29) b)). Ordinal-position semantics also observed via START NOT LESS THAN 4 -> READ NEXT returns RRN 7 record. No spec-derived golden asserts the output-mode numbering starting at 1 (l1_read_relative_key_moved writes with explicit keys 1..3), so test-ref is empty = test-needed. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]
rows.rule-text: All records stored in a relative file are uniquely identified by relative record numbers. The relative record number of a given record specifies the record's logical ordinal position in the file. The first logical record has a relative record number of 1, and subsequent logical records have relative record numbers of 2, 3, 4, ... .

rows.subject: RENAMES clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR7 'Data-name-2 and data-name-3 shall not be subscripted.' cite.py --check 13.18.45.3 -> OK §13.18.45.3 7). BindRenames captures both operands through ClauseDataName, which refuses a subscripted operand (COBOLNET2024) and records it in _refusedClauseOperands so ResolveRedefines skips it (one fault). Probe sr7.cob `66 X1 RENAMES A(1).` -> error COBOLNET2024 at --std 2023 and --std 85. No RENAMES-specific negative golden found under tests/conformance/negative (test-needed). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the RENAMES clause is in every edition; the rule text is the 2023 §13.18.45.3 wording)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-2 and data-name-3 shall not be subscripted.

rows.subject: REPLACE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.2.4.4 "'source text' refers to the conditionally-processed compilation group" -> OK 1). REPLACE runs as Step 3 over the CC+COPY-expanded text (ConditionalCompilationProcessor.cs:85), so text in an omitted >>IF branch is neither a REPLACE statement nor replace-subject text and copybook text is. Probe out/probe/replace-p2/cc.cob / ccok.cob: a REPLACE inside a false >>IF branch has no effect (DISPLAY XX -> 'XX '). No spec-derived golden pins the CC interaction. || editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (REPLACE statement; Annex E 2014->2023 lists no change to it) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ConditionalCompilationProcessor.cs#Process (Step 3); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ApplyReplaceStatements
rows.rule-text: In subsequent general rules of the REPLACE statement, 'source text' refers to the conditionally-processed compilation group.

rows.subject: REPLACE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.2.4.4 "additional spaces may be introduced only between text-words where there already exists a space" -> OK 10). Source is normalized to logical free form before Step 3; pseudo-text-2 is inserted verbatim (its own line breaks/indentation are existing spaces), partial-word-2 is spliced with no added space. Probes out/probe/replace-p2/gr9.cob (multi-line pseudo-text-2 -> A, B) and lead.cob (NEW-X spliced). || editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (REPLACE statement; Annex E 2014->2023 lists no change to it) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ApplyReplacements; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs (normalization to free form precedes REPLACE)
rows.rule-text: The text that results from the processing of a REPLACE statement shall be in logical free-form reference format. Text-words inserted into the resultant text as a result of processing a REPLACE statement are placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format. When inserting text-words of pseudo-text-2 into the resultant text, additional spaces may be introduced only between text-words where there already exists a space or a space is assumed. NOTE 2 A space is assumed at the end of a source line.

rows.subject: REPOSITORY paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.8.3 'If the specified object-class-name-1 is the name of the class definition in which this REPOSITORY paragraph is specified' -> OK §12.3.8.3 5)). Code: OoRepositoryScope.Build walks outward from the reference; at the ClassDefinitionContext it ASSIGNS classes[ownName] = null (resolve by the declared word = the containing class) before Collect() adds that class's own REPOSITORY entries with TryAdd, so a self-named class-specifier (and its AS literal-1) never displaces the self binding. Probe out/probe/repo/sr5.cob (--std 2023): CLASS-ID. S5SELF whose REPOSITORY writes 'CLASS S5SELF AS "S5OTHER"' (S5OTHER is a real group class with a factory MAKE printing WRONG-OTHER-MAKE); S5SELF's factory MAKE does INVOKE S5SELF "NEW"; main prints SELF-HELLO - the self reference reached S5SELF. The code comment at OoNameResolution.cs:127 cites this as '§12.3.8.2 GR5/GR8' (wrong clause; the Build() comment at the same file correctly says §12.3.8.3 SR5/SR8). No spec-derived test pins a self-named class-specifier -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: If the specified object-class-name-1 is the name of the class definition in which this REPOSITORY paragraph is specified, references to object-class-name-1 are to that class definition and this class-specifier is ignored.

rows.subject: REPOSITORY paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.8.3 'If the specified interface-name-2 is the name of the interface definition in which this REPOSITORY paragraph is specified' -> OK §12.3.8.3 8)). Code: the interface twin of SR5 in the same loop - at InterfaceDefinitionContext Build ASSIGNS interfaces[ownName] = null before the definition's own REPOSITORY entries are TryAdd-ed, so a self-named interface-specifier is ignored. Probe out/probe/repo/sr8.cob (--std 2023): INTERFACE-ID. S8IF whose REPOSITORY writes 'INTERFACE S8IF AS "S8OTH"', a method prototype PEER USING an OBJECT REFERENCE S8IF, implemented by class S8CLS; main invokes PEER -> S8-SPOKE, compile clean. The probe is weakly discriminating (a mis-resolution to S8OTH may not have been observable), so the verdict rests on the code read of the SAME loop whose class arm sr5.cob discriminated. No spec-derived test -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: If the specified interface-name-2 is the name of the interface definition in which this REPOSITORY paragraph is specified, references to interface-name-2 are to that interface definition and this interface-specifier is ignored.

rows.subject: REPOSITORY paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.8.3 'references to program-prototype-name-1 are to the named program definition and this program-specifier is ignored' -> OK §12.3.8.3 15)). Code: ProgramPrototypesOf registers every specifier, then OVERWRITES map[u.Name] with SelfPrototype(u) for every containing program definition and, when a specifier names the unit itself, map[unit.Name] = SelfPrototype(unit) - so the specifier (including its AS literal-3) is discarded and the reference activates the named definition by its own externalized name. Probe out/probe/repo/sr15.cob (--std 2023): PROGRAM-ID. SR15P RECURSIVE whose REPOSITORY writes 'PROGRAM SR15P AS "SR15OTH"', with a program SR15OTH in the group; CALL SR15P recurses into itself (DEPTH=1, DEPTH=2) and never reaches SR15OTH - correct. The containing-program half is structurally the same overwrite (a contained program cannot carry its own REPOSITORY, §12.3.3 SR1, so the case arises through the inherited container specifier). conformance:2002/pb237_program_prototype's CONTAINER-BLOCKED line exercises §8.4.6.8's NO-specifier spelling, not a written self/container specifier, so no spec-derived test pins SR15 itself -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: If the specified program-prototype-name-1 is the name of the program definition in which this REPOSITORY paragraph is specified or the name of a containing program definition, references to program-prototype-name-1 are to the named program definition and this program-specifier is ignored.

rows.subject: RESERVE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: §12.4.5.14.2 prints `RESERVE integer-1 [AREA|AREAS]` (RESERVE underlined, AREA/AREAS optional, one of). Grammar `fileReserveClause : RESERVE integerLiteral (AREA | AREAS)?` matches exactly and is a fileControlClauses alternative. integer-1 is governed by §5.5 1) (cite.py --check 5.5 "shall be unsigned and nonzero unless otherwise specified in the associated rules" -> OK); IntegerOperandRules maps FileReserveClauseContext = Nonzero. Probes with the pinned cobol.exe at --std 85 and 2023: `RESERVE 5 AREAS`, `RESERVE 1 AREA`, `RESERVE 3` compile and run (OK); `RESERVE 0 AREAS` -> COBOLNET2386 citing §5.5 1); `RESERVE -2 AREAS` rejected (COBOL0312); `RESERVE 2.5 AREAS` rejected (COBOL0001); `RESERVE AREAS` rejected. cite.py --check 12.4.5.14.2 "integer-1" -> OK. Side observation (not this rule's shape, a §12.4.5.1 SELECT-format issue): a repeated clause (`RESERVE 2 AREAS RESERVE 3`, and equally `ACCESS SEQUENTIAL ACCESS SEQUENTIAL`) is accepted — reported as a dossier gap/lead against §12.4.5.1. No spec-derived test names RESERVE; test-ref empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause and its format are unchanged across editions; no Annex E entry)]
rows.rule-text:
┌ AREA ┐ RESERVE integer-1 │ │ └ AREAS ┘
> **Figure notes (RESERVE clause syntax diagram).** `RESERVE` is underlined in the printed standard (required word); `AREA` and `AREAS` are **not** underlined. The two stacked words are enclosed in brackets, so the phrase is optional and at most one of `AREA` / `AREAS` may be written. No choice indicators appear in this figure.

rows.subject: RESUME statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Procedure-name-1 shall be a procedure-name in the nondeclarative portion of the function, method, or program.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 -> OK §14.9.33.3 3)). BindResume resolves procedure-name-1 through the ONE procedure-operand resolution (scoped to the source element, so a name of another program does not resolve) and refuses a target whose SECTION is declarative (target.IsDeclarative, PB433) with COBOLNET0714. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe: RESUME AT a declarative paragraph (sr3_D2.cob) and RESUME AT the declarative section itself (sr3_D.cob) -> COBOLNET0714; RESUME AT an undeclared name (sr3_X9.cob) -> COBOLNET1639; RESUME AT a nondeclarative paragraph compiles and transfers (gr3b.cob). pb1010_method_declaratives exercises the method arm. No test asserts COBOLNET0714 (searched tests/ for 0714: none), so the row is CONFORMS-but-untested; the needed negative is a declarative RESUME AT one of its own paragraphs.
rows.rule-text: Procedure-name-1 shall be a procedure-name in the nondeclarative portion of the function, method, or program.
